## reference · CMMS software competitor landscape 2026 independent comparison maintenance
* MaintainX is best for mobile-first teams, with a strong mobile app and real-time communication, starting at $20/user/month.
* Limble is best for full-lifecycle asset management, with a comprehensive feature set, custom pricing, and a free basic tier.
* UpKeep leads in manufacturing compliance, with a focus on audit readiness and safety procedures, starting at $20/user/month.
* Tractian offers AI-driven predictive diagnostics with integrated sensor hardware, starting at $60/user/month.
* Coast provides the best value for small teams, with flexible workflows and competitive pricing, starting at $20/user/month.
* Fiix is best for Rockwell Automation environments, with native integration and AI-powered maintenance insights, starting at $45/user/month.
* eMaint integrates directly with Fluke condition monitoring sensors, starting at $69/user/month.
* CMMS pricing typically ranges from free to $100 per user per month, depending on feature requirements and implementation support.
* Essential CMMS features include mobile work order management, preventive maintenance scheduling, asset hierarchy and history tracking, parts inventory management, and reporting dashboards.
* Implementation time for a CMMS can range from 1-4 weeks for basic work order management to 6-12 months for enterprise multi-site deployments.
* When choosing a CMMS, consider the number of users, feature requirements, integration needs, and total cost, including implementation support and training.
* A CMMS can replace spreadsheets for maintenance tracking, automating PM scheduling, centralizing work order tracking, and generating maintenance KPIs.
